why: Within a scenario you want the truck with the most remaining capacity whenever you place the heaviest remaining package; a max-heap of capacities gives that truck in O(log n), and its halved capacity goes back into the heap.
hints: Which package is hardest to place? Place it first, while trucks are still at full capacity.

Sort packages heaviest first. Give each one to the truck with the largest current capacity; if even that truck cannot carry it, the scenario is impossible. Any other truck choice can only waste capacity.
Per scenario: max-heap of capacities (negate in Python). For each package in descending order, check the top, then heapreplace with top // 2. O((n + m) log n) per scenario.
pitfalls: Capacity halves with floor division after every delivery, including odd capacities: 7 becomes 3, then 1, then 0.
Answer each scenario independently; do not reuse a heap mutated by the previous scenario.
Delivering light packages first can make a feasible scenario look infeasible; go heaviest first.
statement:
You manage Amazon's package delivery system. There are t independent shipment scenarios. Scenario i has a list of truck capacities truckCapacities[i] and a list of package weights packageWeights[i].

  • A truck can deliver a package only if its current capacity is at least the package's weight.
  • After each delivery, that truck's capacity becomes floor(capacity / 2).
  • A truck may make any number of deliveries, and packages can be delivered in any order.

Return an array with one entry per scenario: 1 if every package of that scenario can be delivered, 0 otherwise.

Worked example. truckCapacities = [[7]], packageWeights = [[4, 3]].

  • The truck (capacity 7) delivers the package of weight 4. Its capacity becomes floor(7/2) = 3.
  • It then delivers the package of weight 3. Its capacity becomes floor(3/2) = 1.

All packages were delivered, so the answer is [1].
constraints:
• 1 ≤ t ≤ 10^5; total trucks and total packages across scenarios up to about 10^5 each (not stated in the source, which only asks to avoid brute force)
  • 1 ≤ capacity, weight ≤ 10^9
